# Copper Scroll Column 7 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 3Q15 (Cave 3), Col. 7 | **Condition:** Corroded in places; mostly legible

---

**7:1** In the tomb in the Wadi of Kippah,

**7:2** on the road from Beth Tamar to Hebron:

**7:3** buried seven cubits deep —

**7:4** thirty-two talents.

**7:5** In the cave of the ancient tomb at Abel-Shittim,

**7:6** in the open field:

**7:7** dig to a depth of four cubits —

**7:8** six bars of gold.

**7:9** In the underground passage of Horon,

**7:10** in the field:

**7:11** five and one-half

**7:12** talents.

**7:13** In the irrigation channel of [...]

**7:14** vessels of tithe

**7:15** belonging to the lord of the nations —

**7:16** all of it is seventh-year tithe;

**7:17** the remaining seventh portion has been rendered unclean.

---

*LOGOS notes: Abel-Shittim ('meadow of acacias') was the Israelites' final encampment before crossing the Jordan (Numbers 33:49). Its mention extends the treasure network into the Transjordan. Beth Tamar and Hebron define a route through the central hill country. The halakhic classification of tithes — seventh-year (shemittah) and ritually impure — reflects a Temple-era fiscal system. 'Lord of the nations' (ba'al ha-goyim) may be a title or proper name.*
